title: Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: The drum temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
E1 is posted when the NTC or RTD reading the drum air temperature is open. Heating is disabled, and most cycles will not start.

Replace the sensor at the blower housing.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove top panel to access blower housing.

title: Temperature Sensor Shorted
fullDescription: E2 is the shorted-sensor counterpart. Replace the NTC and inspect wiring.
videoSearchQuery: Fisher Paykel dryer E2 sensor short

title: Over-temperature / Safety Thermostat
shortDescription: Thermal cut-out tripped due to high drum temperature.
fullDescription:
E3 is posted when the high-limit thermostat opens, typically due to blocked lint filter or restricted venting. Clean the filter and duct before resetting.

If the thermostat is open after cooling, replace it along with the thermal fuse if fitted.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, replace hi-limit thermostat and thermal fuse.

faq.a: Yes - lint blockage is a primary cause of dryer fires.

title: Heater Fault
shortDescription: Heater did not draw expected current.
fullDescription: E4 indicates the heater element is open or the thermal fuse has blown. Test element resistance before replacing.

faq.a: Heat pump models show different codes - check your manual.

title: Drum Motor Fault
shortDescription: Drum motor tacho missing or drum not rotating.
fullDescription:
E5 is posted when the drum motor does not run at expected speed. A seized drum, broken belt, or failed motor are typical causes.

Turn the drum by hand - if it does not rotate freely, check the belt.

fixSteps.title: Replace belt
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new drive belt if broken.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap motor if belt is fine but drum will not turn.

faq.a: No - no tumbling means no drying.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display and main board are not communicating.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates the serial link between boards has dropped. Loose harness or failed board cause it.

Reseat the harness after a power cycle.

title: Moisture Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The drum moisture sensors read out of range.
fullDescription:
E7 is posted when the conductive moisture sensor bars in the drum return invalid readings. Heavy fabric softener residue or corroded bars are the common causes.

Clean the bars with vinegar and a soft cloth; if E7 returns, replace the sensor assembly.
symptoms: Auto cycles ending too early or late

fixSteps.title: Clean bars
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe moisture sensor bars with vinegar.

videoSearchQuery: Fisher Paykel dryer E7 moisture sensor

faq.a: They leave residue on bars - reduce usage.

title: Condenser Pump Fault (Heat Pump models)
shortDescription: Condensate pump did not empty within time limit.
fullDescription:
E8 is posted on heat-pump and condenser dryers when the condensate pump fails to empty the reservoir. A clogged filter, blocked hose, or failed pump cause it.

Clean the condenser filter and pump intake.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Swap condensate pump if still failing.

whenToCallPro: If pump tests good but drainage fails.
videoSearchQuery: Fisher Paykel dryer E8 condensate pump

faq.a: Vented models don't use condensate pumps - E8 means something different; check your manual.

title: Door Switch Fault
fullDescription: E9 is posted when the door switch reads closed while actuator indicates open or vice versa. Replace the switch after continuity testing.
videoSearchQuery: Fisher Paykel dryer E9 door switch

title: EEPROM / Configuration Fault
fullDescription: E10 signals EEPROM read/write failure. A service-mode reload sometimes works; otherwise replace the control board with one preloaded for the model.

faq.a: User resets do not restore EEPROM.
